parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a purely descriptive, apolitical explainer about how climate scientists gather evidence (ice cores, satellites, CO2 observatories) with vivid precision cues ('a single drop of ink in an Olympic-size swimming pool'). Its main mechanism is boosting perceived competence and, secondarily, openness/transparency about methods; it says little about scientists' motives, funding conflicts, or humility, so integrity/benevolence gains should be smaller, diluting the four-subscale primary outcome. Because it never argues for climate risk or policy, downstream belief/concern/policy effects should be a fraction of the trust effect, propagating only weakly through the trust-to-attitude link within a single sitting. trust_post and belief_post are anchored on pre-treatment answers, which mechanically compresses their ATEs relative to the fresh multidimensional battery measured first. Incentivized behaviors (real dollars, real newsletter sign-up) are notoriously inelastic to a single reading, so I put those at near-zero with slight positive tilt, with a small extra nudge for the AMS donation given the text's meteorological-measurement framing. I calibrated magnitudes to typical single-exposure information interventions in climate/science-trust megastudies: primary trust effects of roughly 2-4 points, distrust reductions somewhat smaller in absolute value, and policy/behavior effects under ~1.5 points.
